title: OIDC trusted publishing is broken by GitHub immutable subject claims
description: release.yml's publish job cannot authenticate to npm. GitHub issues immutable-format OIDC subject claims for this repository (repo:opum-ai@311910387/lore-cli@1365013937:...), and npm Trusted Publishing matches the classic repo:opum-ai/lore-cli:... form, so npm treats the token as unauthenticated and returns E404 on PUT. Proven by decoding a real token minted with audience npm:registry.npmjs.org in probe run 34787200768. Cause is GitHub's 2026-04-23 policy that every repository created after 2026-07-15 uses the immutable format; lore-cli was recreated 2026-09-10, one day after 0.6.0 published successfully from CI under the old repo id. quest-cli is broken identically. Repo-level opt-out does not work: PUT to actions/oidc/customization/sub with use_immutable_subject false is accepted and has no effect. GitHub documents no opt-out once adopted. Until this is resolved every release must use the manual scripts/publish-release.sh path, which itself requires a human because npm demands a browser OTP that cannot be completed in a non-TTY. Full evidence and two documented false leads are on LCLI-475.

acceptanceCriteria.text: release.yml publish job successfully authenticates to npm via OIDC on a real publish:true dispatch, OR the job is removed/replaced with a documented manual-only path and release-publishing.md no longer presents OIDC as the working mechanism

release-publishing.md explains the immutable subject claim incompatibility, including that re-registering Trusted Publishers does not fix it and that the GITHUB_TOKEN Permissions log group omits IdToken even when granted
The npm-side limitation is reported upstream or a tracked upstream issue is linked, so this is not rediscovered from scratch
quest-cli is told the outcome, since its release is blocked by the identical cause
